# Smart Inbox Triage: Stop Sorting, Start Solving

Every support team knows the feeling of opening the queue at the start of a shift and facing a pile of unsorted tickets. Today we're announcing Smart Inbox Triage, a feature that automatically sorts incoming support tickets into four queues: billing, bug, how-to, and account [F1]. The goal is simple: agents stop hand-sorting their morning backlog [F2].

## The problem: triage eats the morning

Support agents at mid-size SaaS companies spend the first 45 minutes of every shift sorting tickets [F3]. That is time spent organizing work rather than resolving it. We heard the same thing from the people who manage these teams: in customer interviews, 9 of 12 support leads named manual triage as their top time sink [F4].

## How Smart Inbox Triage works

A classifier reads each new ticket's subject and body and assigns a queue and a priority (P1-P3) [F5]. Tickets land where they belong, already ranked, so agents can start with the work that matters.

No classifier is perfect, so we built in a way for agents to stay in control. Agents can override any label with one click [F6]. Those corrections aren't wasted, either, because every override is used to retrain the model weekly [F7]. The more your team uses it, the more it learns from your agents' judgment.

## What we saw in the beta

Before launch, we put Smart Inbox Triage in the hands of real teams. The beta ran for 6 weeks with 14 customer teams [F8]. Here is what we measured:

- **Accuracy:** Triage accuracy was 91% against agent-corrected labels [F9].
- **Faster responses:** Median time to first response dropped from 4.2 hours to 2.9 hours [F10].
- **Overrides:** Agents overrode 7% of labels [F11]. Most of those overrides were billing vs account [F12].

That last point is useful to know. Billing and account tickets are the pair most likely to be confused, and the one-click override gives agents a quick fix when that happens.

## What it doesn't do

We want to be clear about the scope of this release. Auto-replying to customers is a non-goal [F16]. Routing to individual agents is also a non-goal [F17]. Smart Inbox Triage focuses on one job: getting tickets into the right queue with the right priority.

## Availability and pricing

General availability is on March 3 [F13]. Smart Inbox Triage is included in the Growth and Enterprise plans at no extra cost [F14]. It is available in English first, with Spanish and German following in Q3 [F15].

## Get your mornings back

Manual sorting has long been a fixture of the start of the support shift, and it doesn't have to be. With automatic queues, priority levels, one-click overrides and a model that learns from your team's corrections, Smart Inbox Triage is built to move agents from sorting to solving. Look for it on March 3 [F13].
